**Question:** How should the tool decide that an output file it is about to write would overwrite one of the input files it was asked to redact? (FR-049)

**Why it matters:** If the check only compares the typed text of the paths, a run like `--out-dir logs` on `logs/app.log` would quietly erase the very log it was asked to redact — the exact silent data loss FR-049 exists to prevent.

**Recommended:** Option A — resolving both paths and comparing the actual file on disk is the only variant that catches all the ways two different-looking paths reach the same bytes (`./logs` vs `logs`, symlinked directories, hard links). It is also the cheapest to test, and Constitution Principle II treats silent data loss as the most expensive failure available.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Treat them as the same file when both paths point to the same file on disk — resolve each and compare the real filesystem object, so differently-spelled paths, symlinks, and hard links are all caught |
| B | Compare resolved absolute path strings only — catches `./logs/app.log` vs `logs/app.log`, but a symlink or hard link to the input is not caught |
| C | Compare the paths exactly as typed — fails only when the two strings are identical character for character |
